data.narrative:
XMOS is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised £200M+ to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector contains 12 total peers (3 public, 9 private), though the immediate peer set is fragmented across different sub-segments and valuations.

Only one valuation method is applicable given available data. Stage-Progression analysis uses the £200M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement, yielding £240M. The Peer-Median approach is not viable: while 12 same-sector companies exist, fewer than three satisfy narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier). Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied because XMOS does not disclose revenue; the three public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trade at a median 21.4x P/S, but without the target's revenue figure, this multiple cannot be translated to an equity value.

The analysis supports a valuation range of £204M–£276M (median £240M), reflecting a ±15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression result. This range remains heavily dependent on the one applicable method and should be interpreted with caution. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data (preventing public-comp triangulation), the heterogeneity of the private peer set, and whether the 1.2x multiplier appropriately reflects XMOS's specific growth trajectory relative to frontier-tech semiconductor peers. Additional disclosure of top-line metrics would materially improve confidence in valuation estimates.
